(2) The mean without the top 5 sessions: sum trade net returns by entry session, drop the 5 entry sessions with the largest sums (a tie is broken by dropping the earlier session first), and take the trade-level mean of the remaining trades. (3) The mean of per-session means: the equal-weighted mean, over entry sessions, of each session's trade-level mean. A synthetic test fixes each on a small table.
sensitivities: two-way (session, symbol) clustering: the trade-level mean with a Cameron-Gelbach-Miller two-way cluster-robust standard error, V = V_session + V_symbol - V_session x symbol, floored at the larger one-way V
validation restricted to symbol-sessions that were not a broad-universe lane decision (exposure_registry.consequence)
table-only cost, and the stress cost
every terminal-zero trade rebooked at the last eligible bid of its hold (populations.terminal_exits)
trades whose hold spans a session flagged by the ratio rule of populations.suspected_unadjusted_split removed

holdout_gate.opens_only_for: Items that passed validation: Holm-adjusted validation p <= 0.05 in the 5-item family, the minimum validation sample (for H1-D, in each group) and, for a tradable cell (H1-D-b_lane-low, H3-a, H3-b), the three robustness statistics. There is no cap: every validated item is carried. A synthetic gate test carries three validated tradable cells including H3-a, and refuses one that fails a robustness statistic.
holdout_gate.no_pass: If nothing validates, the holdout is never labelled or read, and that is the result.
holdout_gate.prospective_collection: The frozen collector collects forward from the session of the freeze: its plan (sessions, symbols, asof, the rename re-fetch) is core/plan.py and its records core/store.py, and only the transport is under study/fetch/ (review round 8, R8-1). Each batch holds screen data only, for the whole enumerated list (universe_and_identity.enumeration, refreshed per batch): the daily bars (raw, split and all) and official prints of sessions s-1 and s for each collected session s, with asof = s, plus corporate-action records. Batches are sealed into a private snapshot whose sha256 is committed per batch with its accrual log. No quote and no minute bar is collected, and nothing selects symbols by membership. Everything else a holdout event needs (lookbacks, minute bars, entry, exit and terminal-search quotes, hold-period prints) is fetched only under a granted 'count' or 'read' entry, by the frozen fetch code with the event's asof = t (universe_and_identity.asof), and sealed before use. Sessions from the freeze to N0 - 1 serve only as lookback inputs. No outcome is computed from any batch before a granted 'read' entry. A batch is timely if its accrual log is reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET of the session after its last session. A session with no timely batch is collected by the next batch, flagged late-collected and counted; it stays in the holdout (collection is not a read), and chronology.holdout.accrual_exposure treats trades that span it as paper-exposed. Because the asof mapping of a renamed symbol may become available only after the rename day, each batch also re-fetches once, logged, the rows of sessions s-1 and s under the new symbol with asof = s for every name_change record effective (process_date) on a session s of the previous batch, and those rows join session s's screen (counted per batch; review round 7, F9). In code (review round 9, H-1 and M-6): each batch is one run of run.py collect under its own committed granted 'collect' authorization. It collects every session from the session after the previous complete batch (the freeze session for the first) through a closed session, refreshes the enumeration into its own snapshot (sealed as <root>/collect-<authorization id>), and its completion record carries the batch's accrual log. A count or read reads every sealed batch through core/holdout_store.py, which merges the screen per (symbol, session): the row of session s for symbol X comes from the latest batch whose asof = s request names X, and the rename re-fetch rows join it. A count or read is refused while any session from N0 - 1 through the window's last session is in no batch. A symbol-session that no batch holds, because its symbol entered the enumeration later, is fetched by the count or read with asof = s and sealed in its snapshot.

The action (collect, count or read) runs only when that record is committed and pushed, because core.runner.context refuses an access log that differs from origin/main, and only under that record (gate.require_granted). It appends its completion record and run-log line even when it fails, and its results file has a fixed path under results/. A 'read' request before the final count and the last terminal-search window writes nothing, unless the read deadline has passed.

study_code.rule: The frozen protocol records study_code = {tree: the git tree hash of blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study/, fetch_tree: the git tree hash of blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study/fetch/}. It pins trees only, never a commit: the repository squash-merges, so a PR-branch commit becomes unreachable, and every run appends run-log, access-log and amendment lines outside the tree, which moves HEAD (review round 7, C5). The study tree is merged to main before the freeze pull request, which does not change it. Every run checks out a commit reachable from origin/main whose blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study tree equals the pinned tree (or a passing transport deviation of it), executes that tree, and reads the logs and data files of that same commit; the commit is recorded as provenance only. The tree holds the study code, the count-only code, the request plan and records (core/), the fetch transport (study/fetch/: HTTP client, authentication, pagination and retry only; review round 8, R8-1), the pinned copies (pinned_copies), the synthetic tests and study/runtime.lock. runtime.lock pins the Python version and numpy, pandas, exchange_calendars 4.13.2 and duckdb (review round 8, E1), with their dependencies. Every fetch and evaluation entry point refuses to run unless the protocol file at its fixed path has status frozen and study_code.tree equals the running tree, and unless study_code.parameters equals the code's parameters (review round 8, R8-4 and R8-2; core/guards.py, core/runner.py). The tree holds no data file (data_files). Every run, fetch and evaluator call names the tree and runtime it ran from. Development, validation and every holdout 'count' and 'read' run from this one tree, and the evaluator refuses any other (holdout_gate.evaluator_refusals). The only tree changes that keep a stage are transport deviations (transport_deviations). Review round 9: every entry point is run.py, run as python -I -B (runtime.lock run_command), which sets sys.pycache_prefix to a fresh directory before any study module is imported, so no bytecode cache in the tree is read; the tree may hold no other ignored file (F9). core.runner.context also refuses unless HEAD is reachable from origin/main and the run log, access log, deviations file and amendment files equal their origin/main content (F2; they are no longer ignored by .gitignore), and it reads the protocol from the freeze commit's blob, refusing a working copy or HEAD that differs from it (F3). A library call that bypasses run.py writes no run-log line, so its result can never govern (F8).

Appending a line never changes the study tree. The run log records each amendment file's sha256 and byte length at every run, and the evaluator refuses a file whose earlier logged content is not a byte prefix of its current content.
run_discipline.run_log: blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/run-log.jsonl, append-only JSON lines. Every run of the frozen automation gets one line: each stage's fetch and re-fetch, development, validation, and each holdout 'count' and 'read', including failed and partial runs. Each line records the utc start and end, stage, purpose, commit run at (provenance) and study tree, runtime lock sha256, protocol_sha256 (review round 8, R8-2; every results file carries it too), data-file sha256s and amendment-file sha256s and byte lengths, input snapshot sha256s, status (complete, failed or partial) and the sha256 of the results file, if one was written (at most one per run, written atomically; run_discipline.once). For the validation results commit, it also records the GitHub-recorded time it became reachable from origin/main. Each line is committed and pushed before the next run of any stage starts.
run_discipline.once: Development is computed by one logged run and validation by one logged run. A run holds every outcome in memory and writes the stage's results as one results file, atomically (temporary file, fsync, rename), only after every item of the stage is computed; no outcome is written before (review round 7, C1). A run that ends before that write has written no outcome and is not governing. It is logged as failed, and the stage may run again from the unchanged frozen tree on the same sealed inputs, each attempt logged; a retry cannot differ from an uninterrupted run, because the computation is deterministic (seeded streams, pinned runtime, sealed inputs). The first run of a stage that writes its results file is the stage's governing run. The governing development run's results are descriptive (multiple_testing.development_screen), and the governing validation run's results file governs the holdout gate. Each holdout 'count' and 'read' writes its results the same way, and each may be retried after a failed run with no results file under chronology.holdout.read_timing (review round 8, R8-6). In code (review round 9, F1, M-4 and F10): each development or validation stage is fetched by one logged run (a second fetch is refused unless every earlier attempt failed and sealed nothing) and evaluated into results/<stage>.json, a fixed path. An evaluation is refused when the stage already has a results line or file, when its snapshot is not the one its fetch line sealed, or when an earlier failed attempt used another snapshot. A run interrupted after its results file was written logs that file's sha256 as complete.
run_discipline.deviations: Any change to the study tree after the freeze is a numbered deviation in blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/deviations.json (cause, diff reference, new tree hash, affected stages), committed and pushed before any run from the new tree. A run from a deviated tree is reported beside the governing result, carries no label, and never governs a stage, the holdout gate or the extension decision. There is no exception for a rerun after a code change, whatever the cause and whatever it reproduces (review round 7, C1 and C2): a stage that cannot complete from the unchanged frozen tree is void. A void development stage reports every item as underpowered there (development gates nothing). A void validation stage voids the holdout of this protocol version (every item scores p = 1 at validation). A void holdout 'count' or 'read' labels every carried item 'not supported (holdout not read)' with the reason (chronology.holdout.read_timing). Transport deviations (transport_deviations) are the only tree changes that keep a stage, and they change no evaluation code.
run_discipline.fetch: Before any outcome of a stage (development, validation, and each holdout 'count' or 'read'), the frozen code fetches every quote window, minute bar, per-event daily bar and official print that stage needs, and for development and validation first the full 2016-2020 screen data (universe_and_identity.request_shapes), under universe_and_identity.asof. Review round 8, R8-1: the request plan (symbols, asof, sessions, stamps, entry, exit, search and backward windows, and the enumeration) is derived by core/plan.py and core/stage.py, in the evaluation tree, only from sealed inputs (the calendar, the enumeration, corporate-action records, decision-time inputs, and the timestamps and eligibility of already sealed quotes); the loop core/driver.py fetches every planned request not yet sealed until the plan adds nothing. study/fetch/ receives one planned request and returns its raw pages; it derives nothing and parses no row. Terminal-search windows of censored trades extend past the segment end (populations.terminal_exits.segment_end), and backward windows follow populations.terminal_exits.booking (R8-7). The result is sealed as a sha256-pinned private snapshot (the ledger's sha256; the ledger holds every page's sha256 and normalized-record sha256), and that sha256 and the stage's fetch-incomplete rate by kind are committed in the run log. At most one re-fetch is allowed: once, of only the fetch-incomplete requests, before any outcome of that stage, followed by fetching any window that only then became plannable, committed the same way. After it, the 1% void rule is final. No outcome is computed from unsealed data.
run_discipline.synthetic_tests: The evaluator refuses a results file whose run-log entry names a tree other than the pinned one, a holdout count or read from a tree other than the pinned one or a passing transport deviation of it, a transport deviation without a passing reproduction check, a runtime that differs from runtime.lock, an edited (not appended) amendment file, a second results file for a stage, a read retry that chronology.holdout.read_timing does not permit, and an outcome computed before the stage's fetch rate is committed. It accepts a run from a commit reachable from origin/main whose study tree equals the pinned tree, with run-log, access-log and amendment lines committed after the freeze. A test kills a run before its results write and asserts that nothing was written and that the retry reproduces an uninterrupted run byte for byte. The suite is study/tests/, run by study_code.test_command under study/runtime.lock. Review round 9 (F6) adds command-level tests against a temporary repository shaped like this one after the freeze (tests/fixture_repo.py), so no test depends on the real protocol's status or writes to the real run log: every command refusing on a draft, a stage fetched once and evaluated into one results file with a kill after the write, the context refusals (bytecode isolation and ignored files, logs off origin/main, a protocol edited after the freeze, amendment timing, coverage_decision, transport deviations), the count-only command, and the holdout path through collect, count with two extensions and read, with two batches of different enumerations and a rename re-fetch, and the not-read label after the deadline.
run_discipline.pinned_copies: The study tree imports no module outside itself except the Python standard library, numpy, pandas, exchange_calendars and duckdb (review round 7, F6; review round 8, E1 adds duckdb, which the pinned dedupe_identity needs). It holds byte-for-byte copies of the external definitions it needs, listed in study/pinned_copies.json as (source path, commit aa6fc79, git blob, sha256, definition names): the Bars class and ET, et_epoch, TIME_BUCKETS, PRICE_TIERS, DV_TIERS, time_bucket, price_tier and dv_tier from mover-early-entry rules.py (R8-12); official_price from sessions_io.py; valid_quote from quotes.py; dedupe_identity with DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SESSIONS, DUPLICATE_SERIES_MIN_SPAN_COVERAGE, CONTINUITY_RATIO, _rename_terminus and _components from broad-universe coverage.py; DATA_SYMBOL from collect_daily.py. A synthetic test reads each source with git cat-file at the listed blob, checks the blob hash and sha256, extracts each named definition with ast (decorators included) and asserts that the copy is identical and holds nothing else. Because nothing outside the tree is imported, a later edit to those paths on main cannot reach a run, and no module-level code of rules.py, quotes.py or coverage.py (their fees.json, protocol.json and duckdb-connection code) ever runs.
run_discipline.transport_deviations: The fetch transport must work against a live API for 12-18 months (review round 7, C2). Review round 8, R8-1: study/fetch/ holds only the transport (HTTP client, host, endpoint path, authentication header, pagination and retry); the request plan, the stamps and windows, the enumeration, response parsing and row filtering are evaluation code outside it, so no change under study/fetch/ can change which prices exist in a sealed snapshot except by failing a request. A deviation that changes only files under study/fetch/ is a transport deviation. Before any run from the new tree, it passes a committed reproduction check against the most recently sealed snapshot of each request kind that exists (or the snapshot of the pre-freeze native dry run, freeze_preconditions): (a) the new tree regenerates the request plan from the sealed inputs and its canonical request records equal the sealed request records byte for byte; (b) every sealed raw page, re-parsed offline, gives byte-identical normalized records (its sealed normalized_sha256), for every page, not a sample; (c) the new transport re-requests the first 200 requests of each kind, in sha256 order of their request records, and their merged normalized records equal the sealed ones (core/transport_check.py). The result is committed in deviations.json with the deviation. A passing transport deviation may govern every later fetch, collection batch, count and read, whose results carry the qualifier 'transport-deviation'. A deviation that touches any file outside study/fetch/, or fails the check, is an ordinary deviation (deviations). Limitation: a change of the provider's response format needs a parser change outside study/fetch/, which is an ordinary deviation. If no passing transport deviation restores collection or fetching in time, the affected sessions are late-collected (holdout_gate.prospective_collection) or the read misses its deadline, and chronology.holdout.read_timing applies. Record format (review round 9, H-2): deviations.json is {"deviations": [...]}, and a transport deviation carries number, kind 'transport', cause, diff_reference, new_tree, new_fetch_tree, affected_stages and transport_check (the reproduction check's result, with passes). core.guards.check_study_tree accepts a running tree other than the pinned one only when a committed entry names it as new_tree and the running study/fetch/ tree as new_fetch_tree, its transport_check passed, and the pinned tree and it differ only in paths under fetch/. Every result from it carries 'transport-deviation'.
